reported.title: Blink toggles twice as fast as specified
reported.description: The half-period constant HALF_MS is 500 (line 6), but the elapsed-time test on line 61 compares an 8-bit millis slice against HALF_MS, so a toggle fires every 500 ms and the lamp changes state twice per 1000 ms cycle. Measured evidence shows D12 toggled 8 times in a 2000 ms window starting at 245 ms (limit 5) and 16 times over the 8.00 s run, i.e. a 250 ms half-period rather than 500 ms. D12 toggled 8 times in a 2000 ms window starting at 245 ms (limit 5), and 16 times over the whole 8.00 s run.

truth.description: byte HALF_MS truncates 500 to 244 so blink period is too short

judge_input.spec:
- Nav beacon LED on D12; quiet hold switch on D3 to ground with internal pull-up (active LOW).
- Blink D12 with 500 ms HIGH and 500 ms LOW while quiet is released, forever.
- Print the exact line `tick` on each rising edge of the beacon (once per 1000 ms ±120 ms).
- While D3 is held LOW, force the beacon OFF and pause the blink schedule.
- Beacon must not change state more than 5 times in any 2000 ms window during free blink.
- Every 2000 ms print `nav rises=<n> quiet=<0|1>` for operator telemetry.
